Embedded & hardware security

External Flash and Firmware Recovery

Planned work on reading SPI Flash and eMMC, recovering firmware and configuration, and examining how external storage affects device security.

To be continued…

Planned scope

This planned series will investigate reading SPI Flash and eMMC devices and analyzing their contents. Future notes will examine recovered firmware, configuration, and stored secrets, with the device setup and limitations documented alongside the analysis.

Draft outline

This is a structured draft. Each section will be completed with measured results, commands, and evidence as the work is carried out.

Flash identification

  • Read the part marking and locate the datasheet.
  • Determine voltage, package, and interface mode.
  • Identify in-circuit access points.

Reading the device

  • Choose in-circuit or desoldered reading.
  • Capture multiple reads and compare hashes.
  • Document adapter wiring and clock settings.

Image validation

  • Check size, erase state, and partition boundaries.
  • Compare against a vendor update image where available.
  • Record any inaccessible or protected regions.

Recovery and analysis

  • Extract configuration and stored secrets with care.
  • Document the filesystem and boot layout.
  • Assess how external storage affects device security.

Restore and references

  • Verify a known-good reflash before returning the board.
  • Keep the original dump read-only.
  • Link datasheets and recovery notes.

Topics to cover

  • SPI Flash
  • eMMC
  • Firmware and configuration recovery
  • Stored secrets and device configuration
